title: Policy Runway + Safe-Swap Config Guardian
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Goal: Implement an automated ‘Policy Runway’ that stages config changes through a safe-swap flow and provides an automated, explainable rollback advisor when safety signals trigger. This ticket bundles the control-plane policy, signal definitions, staged-apply choreography, and a reconciliation service to repair or revert divergent state.
background: We frequently push config changes (batch/window sizes, KV cache params, kernel toggles) that can cause cost spikes or tail-latency regressions. Existing manual rollback is slow and error-prone. The Policy Runway is a bounded window during which a config change can be exercised under synthetic and live curtailed traffic and either promoted, healed, or automatically swapped back to a safe version.
requirements: 1) Define a compact set of deterministic signals for automated rollback: cost-per-token delta, 95/99p latency, error-rate, batch miss-rate, KV cache hit-rate, memory pressure, and model output regression score. 2) Implement staged apply states: Preflight -> Shadow -> SoftSwap -> FullSwap -> Monitor. 3) Provide circuit guardrails: hysteresis, minimum-exposure, max-exposure, and manual hold. 4) Build Reconciliation Service: snapshot/restore with sparse checkpoints and idempotent apply semantics. 5) Expose explainable rollback reasons and an approval UI for manual override.
acceptance_criteria: 1) New runways can be created via API and bound to a config change. 2) Shadow applies route only duplicated requests; no production mutation. 3) SoftSwap can be configured to serve x% of traffic and will auto-revert if safety predicates trip. 4) Automatic rollback executes within 60s of trigger and leaves a traceable audit event. 5) Reconciliation service can restore golden-state snapshot and warm prefix caches within SLOs documented in runtime-1.24. 6) PM/Design and SRE have signed off on thresholds and UI copy.
technical_approach: - Policy Engine: new microservice that evaluates signal time-series with windowing and computes an explainability vector (which signal, magnitude, and confidence). - Staged Apply Controller: reusable finite-state machine implementing Preflight/Shadow/SoftSwap/FullSwap with graceful backoff. - Reconciliation Worker: incremental snapshotter and sparse-prefix warmup with KV quarantine (mark stale caches and trigger async repopulation). - Telemetry: add derived metrics (batch-mismatch-rate, token-cost-delta) and aggregate per-change. - Rollback Executor: transactional config swapper with a fast-path for emergency cutover.
rollout_plan: 1) Internal dogfood: enable for 10% of teams and non-critical models. 2) Monitor synthetic and live signals for two weeks. 3) Expand to 50% and add automated rollback without human approval for P0 signal matches. 4) Full rollout with UI and audit logs after SRE sign-off.
safety_model: - Minimum-exposure: never exceed 5% traffic until 30m post-SoftSwap. - Hysteresis: require a sustained signal for 3 consecutive evaluation windows before auto-revert. - Cost throttle: if cost-per-token increases > 30% and persisting for 2 windows, trigger immediate rollback. - Human-in-loop threshold: certain output-regression alerts require manual confirmation.
state_reconciliation: We will maintain change snapshots in an append-only ledger (small metadata only). Reconciliation Worker will compare desired config, live applied state, and recent telemetry; if divergence is detected it will either perform a safe reapply (idempotent patch) or roll back depending on stability. Sparse checkpoints capture important warmup prefixes for common routes to reduce impact of rollbacks. All reconciliation actions create immutable audit events.
observability: Dashboards: per-change timeline (state transitions, triggers, telemetry overlays), fast filter by model/region/route. Alerts: PagerDuty for emergency auto-rollbacks; low-severity Slack alerts for soft reverts. Suggested KPIs: time-to-rollback, % successful auto-heals, delta in cost-per-token, and regression rate.
security_and_compliance: Config change ledger encrypted at rest using KMS; audit events exported to central logging and retained according to compliance policy. Security review required for the microservice endpoints and RBAC for who can create runways or approve reverts.
test_plan: Unit tests for policy engine windows and explainability output. Integration tests: simulate synthetic traffic with controlled deltas to assert correct SoftSwap behaviour and rollback. Chaos test: inject large latency and ensure automatic rollback executes and reconciliation restores golden-state. Canaries in staging for 48h.
open_questions: 1) Exact default evaluation-window length (30s vs 60s) — prefer 60s for stability. 2) Should we enable auto-revert for cost spikes without manual review? Proposal: allow opt-in at project level. 3) Persistence backend for snapshots: existing config-store vs new append-only S3 ledger (tradeoffs: read latency vs immutability).
implementation_notes: - Reuse existing prefix-warm worker for sparse prefix warmup. - Policy Engine will import the telemetry library changes in PR #4821. - Must coordinate with runtime team for KV-quarantine API (ENG-72654).
